newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/IBM earnings and rebound in techs.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/IBM earnings and rebound in techs.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp options dominated the Chicago Board Options Exchange most-actives list ahead of the firm's earnings due out later in the day, traders said.
Interest was heightened by a rebound in the smaller technology stocks since late Tuesday, they said.

Hank Nothnagel, senior vice president of options trading at EVEREN Securities, said higher than expected IBM earnings would help solidify bottoms for the technology sector, which had been lagging the overall market's recent sharp rebound.
"That (positive earnings) would really help," Nothnagel said, noting that interest was gradually shifting from the less-battered big names to the more beaten-up stocks.
"We're getting some bottom-dippers now," he said. "Hopefully, we'll be able to get interest in some of the lower priced numbers (shares)," he said.
IBM shares were up 3-1/8 at 143-1/8 in late trade.

May 140, 145 and 150 calls were among the heaviest traded calls on CBOE with volume of 4,000 to 5,300 contracts each. May 130, 135 and 140 puts were the three busiest CBOE puts with turnover of more than 5,200 contracts each.
Despite the hefty volume, traders said implied volatilities for IBM's May options were not bid up, generally staying near the stock's corresponding historical volatility slightly above 30 percent.
Nothnagel said implied volatilities in technology stocks remained relatively subdued today, but that volatilities would probably pop up once the stocks started making significant gains.
On the other hand, Jesse Stamer of TradeNet, a CBOE designated primary market maker, expected volatilities to generally calm down after IBM results.
He said anxiety in tech stocks stemmed from earnings uncertainties and that IBM was among the last major hurdles.
Either way, traders generally agreed that the tech stocks had probably put in a bottom, at least for now.

Jay Shartsis, director of options trading at R.F. Lafferty & Co, said Tuesday's reversal in 3Com Corp, U.S. Robotics Corp and Ascend Communications Inc was impressive. Those shares had been hit earlier by news that Intel Corp was entering the networking business.
"Even if they're going to zero, they should rest here for a while, along with other tech stocks," Shartsis said.
Interest in long-suffering shares was also seen in some names outside the technology sector.

On the Pacific Stock Exchange, a fairly large 720-lot strangle traded in Echo Bay Mines Ltd May 5.0 puts and 7.5 calls. The stock stood at 5-11/16, down 1/2 after Tuesday's news that company's chief executive had resigned.
"The company's had a problem for a long time," said a trader on the PSE floor. "I guess it's the tail end of it."
He said the public was on the sell side of the deal to take advantage of the pumped-up premiums. The strangle was priced at a volatility of about 50 percent.
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
